title: Air Gun & Airsoft Gun Manufacturing
one_liner: A small, mature US manufacturing niche serving recreational shooting, hunting, pest-control, training and airsoft-sport demand.
overview: This industry manufactures non-firearm guns that propel BBs, pellets or plastic airsoft rounds using compressed air, gas, springs or electric mechanisms. The 2022 IBISWorld baseline placed 2020 US industry revenue at $291.1 million and forecast 2025 revenue at $305.9 million, implying a slow-growth manufacturing base even while broader consumer airsoft demand is larger. Public 2026 market reports show global airsoft demand at $2.54 billion to $2.8 billion in 2026 and North America as the largest region in 2025, but much of US consumption is supplied by imports and foreign OEM brands rather than domestic factories.

key_stats.market_size: 2026 estimated US manufacturer revenue: about $309 million, extrapolated from the 2022 IBISWorld forecast of $305.9 million in 2025 and 1.0% 2020-2025 CAGR.
key_stats.growth: 2020-2025 baseline forecast CAGR: 1.0%; 2026-2033 global airsoft-guns demand CAGR estimates: 6.96% to 8.4%.
key_stats.employment: 2025 baseline forecast employment: 1,016 workers, up from 975 workers in 2020.
key_stats.trade: 2020 baseline imports: $153.5 million; 2020 baseline exports: $28.2 million; 2025 baseline forecast imports: $155.3 million and exports: $30.3 million.
key_stats.demand_benchmark: 2025 US airsoft-gun demand estimates range from $535.1 million to $788.8 million across public market reports; 2025 global airsoft-gun demand estimates range from $2.38 billion to $2.7 billion.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2022 estimated US manufacturer revenue: about $297 million, interpolated from 2020 revenue of $291.1 million and the 2020-2025 forecast CAGR of 1.0%.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2020 baseline revenue mix: air guns 63.6%, airsoft guns 20.5%, other products and services 15.9%.

how_it_makes_money: Manufacturers earn revenue by selling air rifles, BB guns, pellet pistols, PCP air guns, CO2 guns, electric airsoft guns, spring airsoft guns, ammunition, magazines, optics, accessories, branded replicas and private-label products through sporting-goods retailers, big-box chains, e-commerce channels, specialty airsoft dealers, training users and direct-to-consumer stores.
cost_structure: Major 2020 baseline costs include purchased inputs such as plastic resin, steel, springs, machined components, valves, barrels, seals, CO2 systems, packaging and imported finished goods; wages were $58 million in 2020; profit was $22 million in 2020. Cost pressure in 2026 is tied to plastic resins, metals, freight, compliance documentation and price competition from imported Asian-made airsoft and entry-level air gun products.
major_players: Tokyo Marui, G&G Armament, CYMA and other import/OEM brands
current_dynamics: The US manufacturing niche is steady rather than fast-growing. Premium PCP air guns, licensed replicas, training-oriented products and higher-performance airsoft rifles are healthier than low-end commodity spring products. Demand benefits from the 2024 NSSF-reported base of more than 52.7 million US sport and target shooting participants, but firearm retail weakness in 2025 and intense import competition limit domestic factory growth. CPSC oversight of imitation-firearm markings since 2023 raises compliance expectations but did not create a ban or new technical standard.
whats_growing: Premium PCP air rifles, higher-price hunting air guns, licensed 1:1 replica airsoft products, online sales, airsoft fields and military-simulation use are growing. Public 2026 reports estimate 2026 global airsoft demand at $2.54 billion to $2.8 billion, with North America the largest 2025 region and online distribution forecast to grow faster than offline channels through 2033.
whats_shrinking: Entry-level domestic production is pressured by low-cost imports, while traditional hunting-linked demand is structurally weaker than older peaks. Gearfire reported 2025 same-store new firearm unit sales down about 13% from 2024, a negative adjacent signal for shooting-sports retailers, and NSSF reported 2024 adjusted firearm background checks down 3.5% from 2023.
recent_developments: 2023-06: CPSC began enforcing 16 CFR part 1272 for airsoft and imitation-firearm marking requirements after oversight shifted from the Commerce Department.
2024: NSSF reported more than 52.7 million US sport and target shooting participants in its 2025 edition study covering 2024 activity.
2025-03: NSSF launched a mentorship coalition reporting 62,005 mentors and 557,467 students across shooting sports, hunting and related activities at the end of 2024.
2025-11: CBP updated import guidance stating airsoft guns that are imitation firearms require blaze-orange marking and that state/local rules may vary.
2026-02: Gearfire reported 2025 same-store new firearm unit sales down about 13% from 2024 and forecast another 7%-12% drop in 2026 firearm unit sales.
2026-06: Grand View Research estimated the global airsoft-guns market at $2.6 billion in 2026, up from $2.4 billion in 2025, with North America at 38.0% of 2025 revenue.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is low-growth for US manufacturers but stronger for consumer demand and import-heavy retail. Domestic revenue is likely to track near the baseline 2025-2026 level of about $306 million to $309 million unless premium PCP, hunting, training and branded replica lines offset import competition. Compliance, product differentiation and channel access will matter more than capacity expansion. Through 2033, public demand-side forecasts for global airsoft guns range from 6.96% to 8.4% CAGR, suggesting opportunities for US brands that can capture higher-margin design, licensing, distribution and aftermarket spending even when production is outsourced.
themes: Premium PCP and high-performance air guns
one_sentence: US air gun and airsoft gun manufacturers sell spring, pneumatic, CO2, PCP and electric products into a market supported by shooting-sports participation and online retail, but constrained by imports, input-cost volatility and rising compliance scrutiny around look-alike firearms.
